title: Implement 3D/BIM authoring workflow on the verified CAD/BIM foundation
objective: Deliver a real 3D/BIM authoring workflow on the verified shared CAD/BIM product (Architecture v1.1): stories/storeys as level containers, walls, slabs, openings, doors/windows and spaces as canonical BIM elements with engine-independent semantic properties, parametric primitives (box, cylinder, extrusion-derived solids) and basic transforms/booleans realized through the existing real OCCT geometry adapter, 3D selection/move/copy/delete/property editing through the existing document command model with immutable revisions and deterministic replay, save/open persistence preserving geometry, semantic properties, identities and lineage, Construction Graph mapping/provenance for authored BIM elements with observed-semantics labels, standard 3D camera states shared by both hosts, and Web/Electron parity for a representative building workflow through the shared App API. The acceptance bar is the actual authoring workflow, not a visual mockup.
acceptance_criteria: A representative building can be authored from stories, walls, slab, openings, doors/windows and spaces through the shared App API in both hosts.
Geometry is produced by the existing real OCCT adapter without direct engine imports in domain/renderer code (LOCK-018 static scan extended to the new BIM core).
BIM semantics and geometry remain separate concerns: semantic properties are engine-free element state; solids are derived descriptors realized through the adapter.
Engine IDs are provenance only; canonical element IDs remain stable and Construction Graph node identity stays independent of engine ids.
3D edits create immutable revisions and are replayable (verified replay to every revision).
Save/open preserves geometry results, semantic properties, identities and revision lineage (identical content hash, history hash and graph events hash).
Web and Electron produce equivalent semantic model results through their real transports.
Existing 2D drafting, real-engine and Graph tests remain green.
New deterministic 3D/BIM tests with declared tolerances are reproducible in CI on the OCCT toolchain.
Unsupported semantic/geometry operations fail explicitly with typed errors; no silent approximation.
No protected architecture paths are modified.
non_goals: Full IFC round-trip implementation (COMPAT-IFC-001 remains downstream).
Project/scheduling implementation or research (explicitly deferred by the Architect).
Live recomputation of downstream quantities on BIM edits (the impact cascade remains an explicit query).
Free-form solid modeling beyond the declared primitive/descriptor vocabulary.
Approval or verification claim by implementation.
risk_assumptions: Issue #39 + directive comment 5430962929 are the authoritative scope. DIVERGENCE FLAG: the spec/work-items.md roadmap names this slice COMPAT-BIM-001; the GitHub issue and directive name it COMPAT-CAD-002. Following the established precedent (issue is authoritative, divergence flagged — never silently reconciled), the record id is COMPAT-CAD-002.

DIVERGENCE FLAG (dependency registry): spec/dependency-graph.md lists the roadmap BIM item as depending on RESEARCH-CAD-007 and COMPAT-CAD-001. COMPAT-CAD-001's PR #38 is MERGED at 9b27d16f264c665b5c9f46999e9f70e75756705c — the exact branch base of this slice — so the substantive dependency is physically satisfied; however its work-item record on main is still PR_OPEN pending the Architect's close-out (MERGED/VERIFIED transitions are architect-only per LOCK-004), and rules.ts requires every declared dependency of an execution-state record to be VERIFIED. Declaring COMPAT-CAD-001 in this record would trip the execution dependency gate and redden governance CI. The record therefore declares RESEARCH-CAD-007 (VERIFIED) and flags the roadmap divergence for the Architect instead of silently reconciling it.

Stories are canonical BIM ELEMENTS (kind 'bim'), not a layer-table-like structure: story membership is carried by each hosted element's storyId property (single source of truth, replay-safe), story deletion is rejected while hosted elements reference the story (removeLayer precedent: no silent cascade), and wall/slab/space plan coordinates are story-local XY with world Z = story.level + baseOffset, so moving a story is a single-element edit whose derived geometry follows deterministically.

Openings are hosted voids parametrized along the host wall axis; door/window elements fill openings and carry no own geometric position (their solids derive fully from the referenced opening), so moving an opening deterministically moves its fills. Opening moves are supported ALONG the host axis (plus sill shifts); cross-axis components are rejected with a typed error (explicit failure, no silent approximation).

Copy and delete of a host cascade to its hosted openings and fills. This is a declared, itemized cascade (every created/removed element id is reported in the command response and recorded in the revision delta — nothing silent), not the removeLayer-style rejection: a wall copy without its hosted voids would not be a faithful duplicate, and a wall deletion leaving orphaned voids would corrupt the model. The behavior is documented and asserted exactly in tests.

Opening cut tools overhang the host wall faces by a declared OPENING_CUT_OVERHANG (1 mm per side) so the boolean cut removes the full wall thickness without coplanar-face tolerance dependence; the overhang lies strictly outside the wall solid, so resulting volumes are exact (wall L*W*H minus sum of opening W*H*wall-width) and asserted with declared tolerances.

BIM geometry realization is two-phase by design: bim.createElements adds engine-free semantic elements (engineId null, no meshToken); bim.buildGeometry derives descriptors (pure TS), realizes them through the bound geometry adapter, and attaches meshToken/bbox/engine provenance via ONE atomic versioned batch — so engine provenance is itself an immutable, replayable revision. Element.engineId stays the frozen creation-time field; realized provenance lives in props (meshToken + geometryEngine) and the Construction Graph uncertainty labels gate on it.

Graph bridge upgrade is bim-mark-gated: only elements carrying props.bim === true can flip semantics to OBSERVED (authored semantics are extracted by a pure engine-free extractor) and geometry_provenance to OBSERVED (meshToken attached by a realized build revision). Every pre-existing corpus element (including kind:'bim' elements without the mark) keeps byte-identical uncertainty labels and events hashes.

The BIM core (src/bim) is added to the LOCK-018 forbidden-import scan set, exactly like src/drafting in COMPAT-CAD-001; the extrude primitive extends the EXISTING GeometryDescriptor vocabulary and OCCT worker recipe additively (no new engine boundary, no architecture version change); the reference adapter gains an exact extrude class (Z-preserving affine) and typed declines outside it, so the second engine stays usable.

Space areas are computed deterministically at creation (shoelace over the footprint, like drafting dimensions measure at creation) and recomputed only on explicit footprint property edits; no live parametric recomputation (explicit non-goal).

The 3D viewport in both hosts is a bounded deterministic projection: standard camera states (iso/top/front/right) derive from the shared pure camera module + the model's derived world bounding box; the Electron smoke exercises the real BrowserWindow UI, the Web CI smoke drives the same handler chain over the real HTTP transport, and Web/Electron parity is proven at the semantic layer (identical content/history/events hashes through the real transports), not by pixel comparison.

bimSettings (camera preset) is non-versioned persisted workspace state mirrored from the draftingSettings precedent (included in the parity content hash, excluded from revision content hashes), so legacy snapshots open unchanged.

CORE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN-SLICE (documented for the record): undoing a patch that ADDED a prop key (e.g. the meshToken attached by bim.buildGeometry) used to produce an updateElement inverse carrying literal undefined previous values, which serialized as invalid JSON and broke every later save/open. Fix: key-adding patch inverses are now full setProps inverses (exact restoration incl. key removal), and canonicalStringify rejects undefined outright (LOCK-007 hardening). Pre-existing-key inverses keep the classic updateElement shape — byte-identical to all recorded histories. Found by the Electron smoke, pinned by app/test/bim-workflow.test.ts regressions.
CAD-IMPLEMENT-001/002 remain at PR_OPEN and PR #30 remains open (existing governance debt, untouched).
Architecture v1.1 is active and frozen; no protected path is modified.
